note: Switch "dinners" (bet B5, docs/council/2026-11-23-two-day-plan.md): a dinner is a scene. You choose who reclines on the couch beside yours, who else comes, and how strong the wine is mixed. Each of the three parts of the evening can bring one moment: friendships, quarrels, secrets that slip, a fight over the couch of honour. Rules, numbers and moments are invention unless a record says history; the sourced pieces are quoted in docs/research/dinners.md. Moments are data: the engine (src/core/dinner.ts) only casts them from the guests and applies their effects.

wines.name: Well watered
wines.label: Well watered: sober talk
wines.text: The wine is mixed with plenty of water, and the talk stays careful.

wines.name: Mixed as usual
wines.label: Mixed as usual
wines.text: The wine is mixed in the usual way.

wines.name: Strong
wines.label: Strong: tongues loosen, tempers too
wines.text: The wine is mixed strong, and the bowl goes round again and again.

moments.name: A shared cup
moments.text: {A} and {b} share a cup and talk late of their families. They leave as friends.
moments.why: guests of one faction at one table

effects.why: they shared a cup at your table

moments.name: An unlikely friendship
moments.text: {A} and {b}, who never had much to say to each other, find they hate the same men. They drink to you, and to each other.
moments.why: two guests who think well of you

effects.why: they found common ground at your table

moments.name: A toast from the couch beside yours
moments.text: {H} rises on the couch beside yours and pours the libation to your health, before the whole table.
moments.why: the place of honour, given and taken well

moments.name: A cold guest of honour
moments.text: {H} takes the couch beside yours, but eats little and says less. The grudge is still there.
moments.why: an honour does not wipe out a wrong

moments.name: A grievance aired
moments.text: Deep in the wine, {a} says too loudly what the table already knew: you did a wrong that is not forgotten.

effects.why: a grievance aired at your table

moments.name: A careless word
moments.text: {A} lets slip a name that should not have been said at your table, then laughs too quickly.

moments.name: Another man's secret
moments.text: {A}, pleased with the wine, tells a story about {b} that was never meant to be told. You hear it too.
moments.why: a story told across the couches

moments.name: If I ruled
moments.text: {A} talks, half in jest, of what would be done differently if the city had another master. {B} listens closely. You were right to keep an eye on your clever friends.
moments.why: a political rival with wine in him

effects.why: they found they want the same thing

moments.source: Plutarch, Dion 9 (the elder Dionysius on his clever friends); the scene is invention

facts.text: Dionysius I distrusted his clever friends.
facts.quote: he was on his guard against his friends who were men of sense, because he knew that they would rather be tyrants than subjects of a tyrant

moments.name: An insult across the couches
moments.text: {A} mocks {b} before the whole table, and {b} answers in kind. Everyone looks at you.
moments.why: sharp words between men of different factions

moments.name: Two men, one office
moments.text: {A} and {b} both want the same office, and both know it now. The talk between their couches turns cold, then ugly.
moments.why: two men who want the same thing

moments.name: A quarrel mended
moments.text: {A} and {b}, seated near each other, clasp hands over the bowl and put their old quarrel aside.
moments.why: an old quarrel, and wine enough to forgive it

effects.why: they made peace at your table

moments.name: The couch of honour
moments.text: Before {h} can lie down, {a} has taken the couch beside yours, smiling, as if it were the obvious place.
moments.why: {a} wants to be seen next to you

moments.name: The bravest man alive
moments.text: Over the wine you ask the table who is the bravest man alive. The others say your name. {A} does not.
moments.why: a guest who will not flatter
moments.source: Plutarch, Dion 9 (Dionysius I angry with Plato); the guest and the choices are invention

facts.text: Dionysius I was angry with Plato for not calling him the bravest.
facts.quote: the man who was angry with Plato because he would not pronounce him the most valiant man alive

moments.name: Searched at the door
moments.text: Your guards stop {a} at the door: no one comes near you unsearched.
moments.why: an enemy invited to your table
moments.source: Plutarch, Dion 9 (no one came to Dionysius I unsearched, not even his brother); the guest and the choices are invention

facts.text: Even his brother and son were stripped and searched.
facts.quote: Neither his brother nor his son could visit him in his apartment wearing any clothes they pleased, but every one had to take off his own apparel before entering and put on another, after the guards had seen him stripped

moments.name: Your own tongue
moments.text: The wine works on you too. You say what you really think of {x}, who is not at the table. {A} remembers every word.
moments.why: the wine, and a host who drank it

effects.why: {a} carried your words from the table

asks.name: An insult at your table
asks.text: {A} has mocked {b} before your guests, and {b} has answered. The table waits for you.

effects.reason: you laughed at him at your own table

effects.why: sent home together, they laughed at you instead

choices.label: Call for more wine and change the subject

asks.name: Someone on the couch of honour
asks.text: {A} lies on the couch beside yours, the place you meant for {h}. {H} stands waiting.
asks.why: the couch of honour is worth fighting for

effects.reason: you sent him from the couch of honour before the table

effects.why: {a} took it, and you let it stand

choices.label: Laugh, and make room for both

effects.why: {a} took it, and no one stopped it

asks.name: The bravest man alive
asks.text: {A} will not call you the bravest man alive. The table has gone quiet.
asks.why: a guest who will not flatter

effects.reason: you raged at his honest answer

effects.why: the court sees what honesty costs

choices.label: Praise the honest answer, and reward it

facts.text: Dionysius I was angry with Plato for not calling him the bravest.
facts.quote: the man who was angry with Plato because he would not pronounce him the most valiant man alive

invented: every choice but anger, and every effect

asks.text: {A} waits at the door between your guards, and they look to you.

choices.label: Strip and search, as for your own brother

effects.why: no blade comes near you unseen

choices.label: Turn the guest away after all

effects.reason: you invited him to dinner and turned him away at your door
